raw_case_text:
An 82-year-old male patient with a past medical history of hypertension, mild chronic kidney injury, and chronic hepatitis C infection with liver cirrhosis was referred to our aortic outpatient clinic due to an arch aneurysm with a maximum diameter of 68mm (Figure 1) and a recent diagnosis of syphilis infection. The patient's serum tests were positive for Treponema pallidum antibodies (by the T pallidum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay method) and he was undergoing treatment with Benzathine penicillin. Other viral markers were negative. The patient was considered unfit for an open aortic arch replacement because of his comorbidities. A total endovascular aortic arch repair was proposed, and a custom-made stent-graft was ordered. At that time, a diagnosis of tertiary syphilis complicated by an aortic arch aneurysm was made.
After 55 days, while waiting for the stent-graft to be manufactured, the patient came to the emergency department with hemoptysis, sudden chest pain, and a history of syncope. At admission, he was hemodynamically stable, with blood pressure of 110/70mmHg and a heart rate of 105 beats/min. Initial blood tests revealed a serum hemoglobin level of 8.9 g/dL, with no leukocytosis but C-reactive protein (CRP) of 221.1 mg/L. Cardiac complications were ruled out with a normal electrocardiogram (ECG) and no increase in troponin levels. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed the aortic arch aneurysm diameter had increased to 95mm from the origin of the brachiocephalic trunk to the upper descending aorta. (Figure 1) Signs of contained hemorrhage into the aortic wall from the vasa vasorum, aortic wall thickening, and multiple ulcer-like projections of the aortic lumen were identified (Figure 2). In this urgent setting, the patient was transferred to the operating room, and the vascular surgical team decided to perform a hybrid arch repair with debranching of supra-aortic vessels and thoracic endovascular aneurysm repair (TEVAR).
A median sternotomy was performed under general anesthesia and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) monitoring, exposing the ascending aorta and arch vessels (Figure 3A). The proximal portion of a 12/8/8 x 300mm Hemashield trifurcated graft (Maquet, Rastatt, Germany) was anastomosed to the ascending aorta using a side-clamping technique. The 12mm distal branch was anastomosed to the brachiocephalic trunk (BCT) and the distal 8mm branch anastomosed to the left common carotid artery (LCCA) in an end-to-end fashion. Both BCT and LCCA were then ligated at their respective origins (Figure 3B). The left subclavian artery (LSA) was embolized using a 14 mm Amplatzer Vascular plug II (AVP II, St. Jude Medical, St. Paul, MN) through a left radial artery access, due to its highly posterior origin. Following this, through the right femoral artery and using rapid pacing, TEVAR was performed from zone 0 to the descending thoracic aorta using a Zenith Alpha thoracic stent graft (Cook Medical, Bloomington, Ind.). Control intraoperative angiography showed complete exclusion of the aneurysm (Figure 4).
The immediate postoperative day was uneventful, except for initial signs of left arm ischemia (pallor, pain, and paresthesia), for which it was decided to perform a left carotid-subclavian bypass using a 6mm Dacron graft. The patient remained hemodynamically stable in the postoperative period and was discharged on postoperative day 11. Six-month follow-up CTA showed complete exclusion of the aneurysm and no other aneurysm formation was observed in the remnant aorta (Figure 5). The following month, the patient was brought to the emergency room in cardiac arrest. Unsuccessful cardiopulmonary resuscitation maneuvers were performed. An autopsy showed cardiac tamponade due to rupture of the ascending aorta at the site of the debranching graft anastomosis.
This manuscript is in compliance with the Helsinki Declaration and with local ethical guidelines. The patient's relatives consented to publication of this report.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 82-year-old male under penicillin treatment for a 68-mm syphilitic aortic arch aneurysm presented emergently 55 days later with acute hemoptysis, sudden chest pain, and syncope due to rapid aneurysm expansion to 95 mm and contained rupture.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially referred to the outpatient aortic clinic with a 68-mm syphilitic aortic arch aneurysm and deemed unfit for open arch replacement (awaiting manufacture of a custom-made fenestrated/branched endovascular stent-graft while receiving benzathine penicillin), the patient presented to the emergency department 55 days later with acute hemoptysis, sudden severe chest pain, and syncope.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of hypertension, mild chronic kidney disease, Child-Pugh cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C virus infection, and recently diagnosed tertiary cardiovascular syphilis on benzathine penicillin therapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for acute chest pain, hemoptysis, and syncope. Home medication: benzathine penicillin.

objective.physical_examination: On emergency admission, blood pressure was 110/70 mmHg and heart rate was 105 bpm. Postoperatively on day 1, he developed acute left upper-extremity ischemia (pallor, pain, and paresthesia).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed anemia (hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL), markedly elevated CRP (221.1 mg/L), normal WBC count, normal troponin, and normal ECG.
objective.advanced_workup: Emergency CT angiography (CTA) demonstrated rapid expansion of the aortic arch aneurysm from 68 mm to 95 mm (extending from the brachiocephalic trunk origin to the upper descending thoracic aorta), with aortic wall thickening, multiple ulcer-like luminal projections, and contained intramural/periaortic hemorrhage from the vasa vasorum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed tertiary cardiovascular syphilis with a rapidly expanding 95-mm ruptured aortic arch aneurysm, established via positive serum Treponema pallidum ELISA antibodies and characteristic vasa vasorum intramural hemorrhage and aortitis on CTA. Underwent urgent hybrid aortic arch repair via median sternotomy: ascending-to-brachiocephalic and left common carotid artery debranching using a 12/8/8 x 300 mm Hemashield trifurcated graft, Amplatzer plug embolization of the left subclavian artery, and Zone 0-to-descending-aorta TEVAR (Zenith Alpha stent-graft), followed on POD 1 by a left carotid-subclavian 6-mm Dacron bypass for left arm ischemia. Discharged on POD 11 with complete aneurysm exclusion on 6-month CTA, but died suddenly at month 7 from cardiac tamponade secondary to ascending aortic rupture at the proximal debranching anastomosis.
